_note: Executable spec for RecommendationEngine. Amounts CAD unless stated. Expected values are exact engine outputs (unrounded beyond 4dp); UI rounds to cents at display. Valuations: MR pinned to 1.8¢ by pinnedValuations below (owner-state.json now ranks at the 1.0¢ floor), MBNA 1.0¢, Bonvoy 0.8¢, cash 1:1, CT ×0.95, CRO ×1.0 auto-sold / ×0.8 held. Default card wealthsimple-vip; threshold both(0.5pp, $0.25). Base owner state per owner-state.json: rogersEligibleServiceLinked=false, cryptoLevelUpProActive=false, Tangerine treatAsAllSelected (2% hypothetical everywhere — can only tie WS, never clears threshold), Scotia 4% cap progress $12,500. Ties rank the default card first.

pinnedValuations._why: These 12 cases document ENGINE BEHAVIOUR and are pinned to an above-floor MR value so they exercise points-vs-cash ranking. They deliberately do NOT track owner-state.json, whose live setting is the 1.0¢ cash floor — otherwise every valuation change would re-baseline the whole spec and the temptation would be to accept engine output rather than re-derive the arithmetic.

cases.description: Standalone grocery (Loblaws), $100, MCC 5411, all networks accepted

expected.notes: Default WS (Visa) gated out by acceptance. MBNA grocery 5x does NOT fire (5300 ∉ {5411,5462,5499}); Triangle grocery excluded by merchantExclude AND MCC. Rogers 1.5% = $3.00 (service not linked). With rogersEligibleServiceLinked=true, winner value becomes $4.00.
250 MR × 1.8¢. Platinum dining 2x = $1.80 — three Amex cards ranked correctly against each other.

cases.description: Grocery $100 with cobalt-eats-monthly progress $2,450 — purchase straddles the cap

expected.notes: Prorated: $50 in-cap × 5 + $50 over-cap × 1 = 300 MR × 1.8¢ = $5.40. Cobalt still edges MBNA by $0.40.

cases.description: Grocery $100 with Cobalt monthly cap fully consumed — winner must flip

expected.notes: Cobalt post-cap 1x = $1.80. THE killer feature: the silent winner-flip a human can't track.

cases.description: Netflix subscription $15.49, MCC 5968, network recurring indicator set, online

expected.notes: Cobalt 3x: 46.47 MR × 1.8¢ = $0.8365. MBNA digital-media 5x (5968) $0.7745. Momentum recurring 4% = $0.6196. Advantage over WS $0.5267 → 3.4pp — clears both thresholds.

cases.description: US$ online purchase ≈ C$165, all networks, Level Up Pro inactive

expected.notes: WS 2% no FX. Rogers USD 3% − 2.5% FX = $0.825 net. Cobalt nets NEGATIVE: $2.97 − $4.125 FX = −$1.155. Crypto excluded (Pro inactive).

cases.description: Same USD purchase with Level Up Pro active and CRO auto-sold

expected.notes: 3% × $165 × 1.0 (auto-sold), 0% FX (pre-2026-09-01 rule), under US$2,500 monthly cap. With croHandling=hold: $4.95 × 0.8 = $3.96 — still wins but narrower.

cases.description: Marriott property direct charge, $300, all networks

expected.notes: 1500 Bonvoy × 0.8¢ = $12.00 vs Platinum travel 2x: 600 MR × 1.8¢ = $10.80. Close race is intentional — tests valuation sensitivity (Bonvoy at 0.6¢ low flips the winner to Platinum).

cases.description: Canadian Tire store, $150 pre-tax, all networks — drawer card should still win with warning

expected.notes: 4% × $150 = 6.00 CT × 0.95 usability = $5.70. Drawer status must surface as a warning ('bring the Triangle'), not suppress the win — per dossier §4.

cases.description: Pharmacy $30, MCC 5912, Tangerine categories unset — nothing beats the default

expected.notes: Best challenger is Cobalt 1x = $0.54 (1.8%) < 2%. Tangerine (treat-as-all-selected) hypothetically ties at 2% = $0.60; ties rank the default first, so WS still wins. Recommendation reads 'stay on your default.'

cases.description: Taxi $12, MCC 4121 — Cobalt technically wins but fails the $0.25 floor

expected.notes: Cobalt 2x transit: 24 MR × 1.8¢ = $0.432; advantage $0.192 = 1.6pp ≥ 0.5pp BUT < $0.25 → 'both' semantics holds the default. This case distinguishes both-vs-either — under 'either' the winner would be Cobalt. Explanation should still show Cobalt as 'marginally better, not worth the wallet dig.'
